title: Defective Verbs (Al-Fiʿl al-Nāqiṣ)
source: Original instructional lesson authored for this application (syllabus ref: Haywood & Nahmad Ch. 29; Ryding Ch. 22 §22.7)
objectives: Identify defective verbs ending in weak radical و or ي (دَعَا, رَمَى, رَضِيَ).
Apply jussive/imperative apocopation (complete deletion of the final weak letter).
Decline defective nouns and active participles (قَاضٍ / القَاضِي).
recallPrompt: From Chapter 16: What are the three jussive signs across sound, afʿāl al-khamsah, and weak-final verbs?

sections.heading: Final Weak Radical (Wāw or Yāʾ)
sections.body: Defective verbs (al-nāqiṣ) end in و or ي. In the 3ms past, و-final verbs are written with tall alif (دَعَا 'he called' from د-ع-و), while ي-final verbs are written with alif maqṣūrah (رَمَى 'he threw' from ر-م-ي). In the imperfect, they end in a long vowel (يَدْعُو, يَرْمِي, يَرْضَى).

sections.label: Jussive Deletion (Ḥadhf Ḥarf al-ʿIllah)
sections.summary: In the jussive (e.g., after لَمْ) and imperative, a defective verb DELETES its final weak letter completely, leaving only the preceding short vowel: لَمْ يَدْعُ (lam yadʿu), لَمْ يَرْمِ (lam yarmi), لَمْ يَرْضَ (lam yarḍa).

sections.translation: The archer did not shoot the arrow.
sections.irab: لَمْ: حَرْفُ نَفْيٍ وَجَزْمٍ | يَرْمِ: فِعْلٌ مُضَارِعٌ مَجْزُومٌ بِحَذْفِ حَرْفِ العِلَّةِ | الرَّامِي: فَاعِلٌ مَرْفُوعٌ بِضَمَّةٍ مُقَدَّرَةٍ
sections.notes: Notice both defective forms: يَرْمِ loses final ي in the jussive, while الرَّامِي has an estimated (muqaddarah) ḍammah on ي.

sections.heading: Subjunctive Keeps the Final Weak Letter
sections.body: In the subjunctive (لَنْ يَدْعُوَ, لَنْ يَرْمِيَ), the final و and ي stay and take a visible fatḥah!
